title: Flux Kiddo
tagline: Kids-focused Fluxstore storefront customized for a family retail catalog.
overview: Flux Kiddo is a client storefront built on Fluxstore Multi Vendor and tailored for a kids/family catalog — navigation, merchandising, and theme work rather than a from-scratch commerce engine.
problem: The merchant needed a mobile shop that felt like a kids brand, not a generic Fluxstore demo, without paying for a full custom commerce stack.
solution: I forked and customized Fluxstore: kids-oriented information architecture, catalog presentation, and vendor/admin flows the merchant actually uses.
architecture: Flutter Fluxstore client talking to a WooCommerce/WordPress backend, with theme and module overrides kept in the kiddo repo so upstream updates can still be merged carefully.
features: Kids-oriented catalog browsing and product detail
Checkout and cart flows inherited from Fluxstore, restyled
Vendor/admin customizations for the merchant's catalog
challenges: Keeping merchant-specific UI without forking so hard that Fluxstore updates become impossible
Explaining honestly that this is a production customization, not a greenfield commerce platform
lessonsLearned: Theme and module boundaries matter more than rewriting Fluxstore internals
futureImprovements: Documented upgrade path for the next Fluxstore release
results: Shipped a branded kids storefront the merchant can operate from the existing Fluxstore/Woo stack
